title: The run panel: a box for what the agent said, a row for what it did, a spinner while it thinks
name: The run panel: a box for what the agent
description:
apps/dashboard/src/logs/Logs.tsx renders every line identically: an `<ol>` of `<li className="flex gap-3">`, a coloured mark, and `whitespace-pre-wrap` text, the whole scroller set in 13px mono. A paragraph the agent wrote to the human and a one-word tool name get the same treatment, which is why the panel is hard to read — there is no visual difference between the two things a reader is looking for.

Three changes, all inside the scroller:

**A box for the agent's messages.** Lines of kind `text` (and `answer`, which is the human's half of the same conversation) render as a contained block — the surface token, a border, radius, padding, and the UI font rather than mono, since prose in a monospace column is the other half of why this is hard to read. Bounded width so a long paragraph does not run the full 980px of the overlay. The two directions must stay distinguishable; `answer` already has its own mark pointing the other way.

**A row per tool call.** Tool lines stay compact, one line each, with the glyph and treatment the vocabulary node defines. They are the texture a reader skims past, not the thing they stop on.

**A spinner while it thinks.** A thinking line renders with a running indicator rather than a static mark. It has to stop: when the next line of any kind arrives, that thinking line is over and its spinner must settle into a resting state — an animation left running is a screen that claims the agent is still thinking after it has answered. Reuse the animation already in this file: `Status` renders `animate-pulse` on a dot for the running state.

Hold everything the file already gets right: the `following` ref and `atBottom` (a reader who scrolled up is reading something), the three-state `Status`, the answer footer, and the index-as-key on an append-only log. Update Logs.test.tsx in the same node.

brief.approach:
Score 4: one component, three render shapes, and one animation that must be able to stop. The vocabulary it renders already exists — do not redecide any of it.

**What it renders from.** `one-mark-colour-and-icon-per-kind-and-pe-6tsw` merged: `apps/dashboard/src/logs/data.ts` holds `MARK`, `TONE` and the `TOOL` glyph table with its fallback, and the kinds now include `thinking`, `check` and `checked`. This node reads those tables and adds none of its own — a glyph decided in a component is a glyph no test can see, which is what `data.ts`'s own doc comment is about.

**Where.** `apps/dashboard/src/logs/Logs.tsx:149-158` is the whole of it today: an `<ol className="space-y-1">` of `<li className="flex gap-3">`, a coloured mark from `TONE`/`MARK`, and one `whitespace-pre-wrap` span — identical for a paragraph the agent wrote and a one-word tool name. Split that `<li>` body on `line.kind` into three shapes, keeping the `<ol>`/`<li>` structure and the `key={index}` (append-only log, the index is stable).

1. **A box for prose — `text` and `answer`.** A contained block: `bg-[var(--surface)]`, a `border-[var(--line)]`, `rounded-[var(--radius-sm)]`, padding, and the **UI font, not mono** — prose in a monospace column is half of why this is hard to read. Bound the width (something like `max-w-[68ch]`) so a paragraph does not run the full width of the overlay. Keep the two directions apart: `answer` is the human's half and already has its own mark pointing the other way, so keep the mark outside the box where both are read in one column — do not give `answer` a different box colour, since colour answers a different question here (ADR 0039).
2. **A row per tool — `tool`.** Unchanged shape: compact, one line, mono, the glyph from `MARK` plus the tool's own glyph from `TOOL` when `line.tool` is non-null. These are texture a reader skims, not something they stop on, so they must stay visually quieter than the box. `check` and `checked` are the same compact shape.
3. **A spinner for `thinking`.** Render the running indicator instead of a static mark. **Reuse the animation already in this file** — `Status` at line 220 uses `h-2 w-2 animate-pulse rounded-full bg-[var(--status-running)]` — rather than importing or inventing one.

**The spinner must stop, and that is the part to get right.** A thinking line is over the moment any later line arrives. So the animation is not a property of the line; it is a property of *being the last line*. Render it as running only when that line's index is the last in `lines` **and** the stream is still live; otherwise the same element with the pulse class dropped. That makes stopping automatic — the next line re-renders the previous one at rest — and it also settles when the run ends, which a per-line timer would not. An animation left running is a screen claiming the agent is still thinking after it has answered.

**Hold everything the file already gets right**, and a reviewer should check each: the `following` ref and `atBottom` (a reader who scrolled up is reading something, and yanking them down is how a live tail becomes unreadable), the three-state `Status`, the answer footer and its `op('answer', …)`, the `ran` line the dispatch node added, and the carried `offset` with its comment about not reconnecting.

**Tests** in `apps/dashboard/src/logs/Logs.test.tsx`, extending the cases already there: a `text` line renders inside a box and a `tool` line does not; a `thinking` line that is last while live carries the running class, and the same line stops carrying it once another line follows; a `tool` line with a `tool` name shows that tool's glyph and an unlisted name falls back rather than rendering blank. Assert on the rendered output, not on the tables — the tables have their own test.

Nothing outside `apps/dashboard/src/logs` changes. `sober-logs-shows-the-same-run-in-the-sam-2lgp` is the terminal's half and is a separate node.

acceptance.proves: prose renders in a box and a tool call does not, a thinking line animates only while it is the last line of a live stream and settles once another line follows, and an unlisted tool name falls back to a glyph rather than rendering blank

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'MARK' -- apps/dashboard/src/logs/Logs.tsx && git grep -q 'TOOL' -- apps/dashboard/src/logs/Logs.tsx && test -z "$(git diff --name-only development -- apps/dashboard/src/logs/data.ts)"
acceptance.proves: the component reads the vocabulary tables and redecides none of it — a glyph chosen inside a component is one no test can see

acceptance.run: git grep -q 'following' -- apps/dashboard/src/logs/Logs.tsx && git grep -q 'atBottom' -- apps/dashboard/src/logs/Logs.tsx && git grep -q "op('answer'" -- apps/dashboard/src/logs/Logs.tsx
acceptance.proves: the scroll-following behaviour and the answer footer survived the rewrite of the line body — the two things this file already gets right
only the run panel changed: no schema, no core, no CLI, no server route, and the terminal's own vocabulary is a separate node
the three render shapes compile against the real LogLine, including its nullable tool
biome and secretlint are clean, including the accessibility rules on the decorative mark and spinner
